question: According to the Reserve Bank of India’s announcement in May 2025, which denomination of the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series banknote, carrying the signature of the new RBI Governor, Sanjay Malhotra, is set to be released?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹20**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** announced the introduction of a new ₹20 denomination banknote in the **Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series**, which is set to carry the signature of the new RBI Governor, **Sanjay Malhotra**, in May 2025.
 
• The ₹20 banknote features a design that aligns with the aesthetic of the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series, which emphasizes enhanced **security features**, durability, and ease of identification.
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series was first introduced in **2016** to replace the older notes and improve security against counterfeiting. The ₹20 denomination continues to be an essential component of this series.
 
• The banknote is expected to showcase the iconic image of **Mahatma Gandhi** on the front, along with features such as a watermark, color-shifting ink, and tactile markings for visually impaired individuals.
 
• The reverse side of the ₹20 banknote typically features motifs representing India's **cultural heritage**. It is likely to retain such elements to highlight the country's diversity and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series:**

 
 
• The series was introduced in **November 2016** after demonetization, starting with ₹500 and ₹2000 notes.
 
• It focuses on enhancing **security features** such as micro-lettering, latent images, and color-changing ink to reduce the risk of counterfeiting.
 
• The notes are designed with **tactile markings** to aid visually impaired individuals in identifying denominations.
 
 
 
• **Features of ₹20 Banknote:**
 
 
• Dimensions: The new ₹20 note measures **63 mm x 129 mm**, making it smaller and easier to handle.
 
• Color Scheme: The dominant color is **greenish-yellow**, providing contrast with other denominations.
 
• Security Elements: Includes features like a **security thread, watermark of Mahatma Gandhi, and electrotype numeral 20**.
 
• Design: The reverse side of the note typically features motifs showcasing India's **cultural and natural heritage**, such as the Ellora caves.
 
 
 
• **Role of RBI Governor:**
 
 
• The **signature of the RBI Governor** is a mandatory feature on Indian banknotes, signifying authenticity and legal tender status.
 
• Sanjay Malhotra, as the new Governor appointed in **2025**, will oversee all aspects of monetary policy and currency issuance.
 
• Governors play a crucial role in ensuring financial stability and introducing innovative reforms, such as updated currency designs.
 
 
 
• **Importance of ₹20 Denomination:**
 
 
• The ₹20 note is widely used for everyday transactions, making it an essential medium for cash-based payments in India.
 
• Its size and value make it suitable for **small purchases**, such as groceries, transportation, and street food.
 
• The introduction of updated ₹20 notes ensures greater security and accessibility for citizens.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Significance of Banknote Series:**

 
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi Series was first introduced in **1996**, featuring Gandhi's image on the front.
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series replaced the older series, incorporating **modern security features and design changes**.
 
 
 
• **RBI's Currency Management:**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is responsible for **currency issuance and management** under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• It ensures the availability of adequate currency notes and coins across the country while maintaining security and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Security Features in Modern Banknotes:**
 
 
• Indian banknotes include advanced security features like **color-changing ink, micro-lettering, and tactile markings**.
 
• These features are designed to prevent counterfeiting and ensure the authenticity of currency.
